subject.title: fix: restore GitHub Copilot turns and account context limits

question: Should OpenClaw accept this shared credential-scoped model/auth boundary across normal runs, compaction, and image resolution as the permanent fix for the GitHub Copilot bug?
rationale: The exact head is technically well-supported, but it changes shared auth-provider and credential-routing behavior beyond the Copilot plugin; repository policy and the protected `maintainer` label require an owner to confirm that this generic boundary is intentional.

options.title: Approve shared boundary
options.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun exact-head checks, and merge if owner review confirms non-Copilot provider overlays and credential isolation remain intact.

options.title: Narrow the runtime change
options.body: Keep Copilot-specific catalog and cache fixes but reduce shared runner changes if maintainers do not want credential-scoped rematerialization as a generic runtime contract.

options.title: Pause for broader design
options.body: Hold the PR if the permanent ownership contract between provider hooks, runtime auth, compaction, and image resolution needs a separate architecture decision.

recommendation.title: Approve shared boundary
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main, rerun exact-head checks, and merge if owner review confirms non-Copilot provider overlays and credential isolation remain intact.

likelyOwner.reason: This person merged both foundational GitHub Copilot changes and is the strongest available owner for accepting a shared runtime/auth contract.
